newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- NOV 1.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Treasury bills snapped up by the buying public ahead of almost certain 8.0 percent taxation by the government. The government will proceed with new taxation measures on which the 1997 budget will be based and the major concern now is how to sell them to the public and to the ruling party PASOK.

--Bank of Greece Governor Lucas Papademos sounds the alarm over the state of the economy in his address to the British Hellenic Chamber of Commerce yesterday, saying that the need to step up efforts to collect revenues, cut back on state spending and to reform the labour market is imperative.
--Public investments programme for 1997 expected to hit the record mark of 1.7 trillion drachmas.

--Brokerage firms holding stocks from the Depositary will be sanctioned if they do not proceed with procedures for shares. The names of the five firms delaying the process have already been given to the bourse authorities.

--Greek construction firms claim German consortium Hochtief is attempting to shore up its profits at the expense of Greek firms in the building of the new international airport at Spata. Greek association requests a copy of the contract.
--High court sets restrictions on construction activity in coastal areas and beaches to protect environment.

--The taxation of bonds and real estate is definite. The government seems to be coming to final decisions on the 1997 budget and all the measures which will accompany it. The issue still outstanding is incomes policy.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is determined to battle internal party differences over economic policy.

--The government weighs the political cost of wiping out tax breaks. Experts from finance ministries, the central bank and commercial banks will examine options for the taxation of financial products.
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou reveals a package of measures aimed at improving the competitiveness and diversifying the tourist product.
--Major changes to state expenditures are in the pipeline and include changes in the management of government bodies, changes in lending to government bodies and taxes for municipalities.
